question: Would you still trust an air raid alert app after this, yes or no?

lines.text: Fake radiation alerts flashed on phones across Ukraine after its Air Alert app was hacked.
Hours later, Russia said its own emergency warnings app was hit by a massive cyberattack.
People in Kyiv and elsewhere got fake radiation, chemical and street fighting warnings.
One message falsely suggested Russia had deployed its Oreshnik missile.
Ukraine's air force told people: there is no radiation threat.
lines.note: Air force on Telegram, via Euronews

lines.text: Spokesman Yuriy Ignat confirmed to AFP the app had been hacked.
Ukraine's SPRAVDI centre blamed Russia. Moscow has not said who hacked its app.
Russia's emergencies ministry said attackers could send false information to the public.
Euromaidan Press says the app had twenty four million downloads by late 2024.
The hacks came as the war's longest truce ended, around Oleshky in Kherson region.
Kyiv says Russia refused to extend the six day pause, brokered by Melania Trump.
Kherson's governor told residents to respond immediately to warnings about Russian attacks.
Would you still trust an air raid alert app after this, yes or no?
